final_candidates.decision_summary: K119 is the catalytic PLP Schiff-base lysine in human CBS; substitution to Ala eliminates covalent cofactor attachment and abolishes catalysis, the most reliable LOF.
D309 in the GVDP motif hydrogen-bonds the PLP pyridine nitrogen, essential for the cofactor electron sink; its removal strongly impairs catalysis.

Proline at the catalytic lysine position both removes the essential PLP-binding residue and adds local backbone rigidity, making abolition of activity near-certain though structurally riskier than the clean Ala variant.

stop_reason.detail: Catalytic-residue LOF candidates are well-supported by mechanistic reasoning and further LLM-only rounds add little without evidence tools.

history.rationale: Lys119 is the conserved catalytic PLP-binding lysine that forms the Schiff base with the pyridoxal cofactor; substitution to Ala abolishes internal aldimine formation and catalysis.
K119 is the catalytic PLP Schiff-base lysine in human CBS; removing it abolishes cofactor covalent attachment and catalysis. Strong LOF candidate.
Proline at the catalytic PLP-Lys position removes the essential ε-amino group and disrupts local backbone, eliminating cofactor covalent attachment and activity.
Loses the essential PLP-binding lysine and adds backbone rigidity likely disrupting local fold; near-certain LOF though slightly riskier than clean Ala substitution.
Thr260 lies in the conserved TSGN PLP-binding motif region; mutation likely perturbs substrate/cofactor binding and reduces activity.
T260 lies outside the canonical PLP/substrate glycine-rich phosphate loop; a conservative Thr->Ala is unlikely to reliably abolish activity.

rejection.reason: T260 lies outside the canonical PLP/substrate glycine-rich phosphate loop; a conservative Thr->Ala is unlikely to reliably abolish activity.

history.rationale: Conserved glycine in the glycine-rich phosphate-binding loop of PLP enzymes; substitution introduces steric bulk that disrupts PLP phosphate anchoring.
Conserved glycines in the TSGN/GTGGT motifs provide backbone flexibility for PLP binding; Ala substitution can rigidify and impair catalysis.
Asn149 is near the catalytic pocket and may coordinate substrate/PLP; disruption could impair turnover.
N149 in the fold II PLP-binding region may hydrogen-bond to cofactor; a moderate LOF candidate retained as backup.
Conserved arginine often stabilizes the phosphate group of PLP; its removal weakens cofactor binding and lowers activity.
Conserved arginines near the active site often coordinate substrate carboxylate/phosphate; removal plausibly reduces activity but effect is less certain than catalytic Lys.
Part of the conserved GNTG PLP-binding loop; alteration may disrupt cofactor/substrate contacts.
Part of the TSGNTG phosphate-binding loop; contributes to PLP phosphate anchoring but single Thr->Ala effect is uncertain.
Conserved glycine within the PLP-binding loop; steric replacement can distort the active-site geometry.
Conserved glycine in the TSGNTGIG phosphate loop; Ala may restrict loop conformation needed for PLP binding.
Residue in the second (CBS) domain region potentially involved in substrate channel; less central but candidate for reduced activity.
S349 is in the C-terminal regulatory region rather than the catalytic core; likely affects AdoMet regulation, not a reliable abolition of activity.

rejection.reason: S349 is in the C-terminal regulatory region rather than the catalytic core; likely affects AdoMet regulation, not a reliable abolition of activity.

history.rationale: The GVDP motif (D residue coordinates PLP) region is critical; targeting conserved D/G here provides an additional active-site LOF hypothesis. WT is G at 307 in the GVDPEG stretch.
Conserved aspartate in the GVDP motif typically hydrogen-bonds the PLP pyridine nitrogen, essential for cofactor electron sink; its removal is a strong LOF candidate. WT is D in the DPEG stretch.
